findings.comment: Electric Service Planning Application submission to Austin Energy and approval documentation not provided in the site plan submittal package or supplementary documents. An ESPA is required before or concurrent with site plan approval for electrical service; verification of submission and approval status cannot be determined from available documents.

Electric Service Availability Letter from Austin Energy Public Involvement has not been provided. Although the site is in Austin's established service territory, this letter may be required depending on AE's standard procedures for new service; its absence cannot be verified as compliant or deficient without clarification of AE service availability determination.

Site plan lacks a note stating that the site lies within the Austin Energy service area. Although four Standard Austin Energy Notes are present on Sheet 3, none explicitly states the service area designation required by AEDC 1.16.0(7). Add a note: 'This site lies within the Austin Energy service area.'

Plans lack the required note stating developer responsibility for designing and constructing all conduit and related electrical infrastructure to current Austin Energy Electric Service Standards, including conductor installation costs and coordination with other utilities. Sheet 3 contains four standard AE notes but does not include this site-specific developer responsibility statement per AEDC 1.16.0(7).

Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design with transformer and pull box locations, but no evidence of Austin Energy approval for these designs has been provided in the documents. Applicability cannot be determined without confirmation that final transformer and pull box designs are required before site plan approval.

No general note found stating that a preconstruction meeting with Austin Energy is required prior to starting demolition. Although transmission easement notes on Sheet 3 mention a 48-hour preconstruction safety meeting requirement, no explicit note in the General Notes or Demolition Plan requires this AE coordination per UCM 3.8.0.

No recorded electrical easement documents or correspondence demonstrating coordination between the applicant and Austin Energy regarding final layout and easement recording have been provided in the application. Verification of easement acquisition and AE coordination status cannot be determined from available documents.

No evidence of a georeferenced AutoCAD drawing submitted to Austin Energy has been provided in the site plan documents or supplementary materials. Verification that the required land development application drawing was submitted to AE with all required content (easements, existing facilities, permanent structures, topology, property lines, building setbacks) cannot be determined from available documents.

Sheet 21 shows transformer and pull box locations but does not depict labeled access routes, truck access dimensions (minimum 12-ft width and 16-ft vertical clearance), or clear paths to proposed AE equipment. Demonstration of unobstructed access for Austin Energy personnel cannot be verified from the available plans.

The site plan shows primarily interior utility infrastructure with water/wastewater connections to existing City mains. Linear footage of public ROW utility construction/excavation and any utility pole relocations are not clearly documented or quantified on the plans. AULCC Completeness Letter not identified in submitted documents. Whether the project triggers AULCC review thresholds (≥300 LF citywide, ≥25 LF in DAPCZ, pole relocations, or main assignments) cannot be definitively determined from available documents.

Cover sheet (Sheet 1) contains only a partial 'Reviewed By' table with spaces for Development Services, City Fire Department, and Austin Water dates. A comprehensive Additional Review Acknowledgement table listing all applicable external reviews and approvals (including TxDOT, railroad, gas company, TCEQ, water districts, MUD, Texas Department of Health, service extensions, and Planning & Development Review approvals) per UCM 2.5.1.F is not present on the cover sheet or identified elsewhere on the plans.

Sheet 3 contains 16 Electric Transmission Notes with detailed restrictions and requirements. However, verification that all eight specific plat notes required by AEDC 1.16.0(8) are present (AE tree pruning rights, additional easement/access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, NESC compliance, 24-hour access, road capacity, 48-hour construction notice) cannot be fully confirmed without reviewing the recorded easement plat. Additionally, confirmation that no portion of the transmission easement is labeled as parkland per AEDC 1.16.0(9) is not verifiable from the current site plan review.

Completeness Check Results show Addressing Review as COMPLETE, suggesting the addressing plan has been reviewed. However, an explicitly documented approved addressing plan from Address Management Services is not provided in the supplementary documents reviewed. Verification of formal addressing plan approval (distinct from an Address Validation Letter) cannot be confirmed from available documentation.
